_purpose: The checked-in rules for the one universal merge rule (LAN-209). A pull request leaves draft exactly once, as the last act of the work, and that act is the authorization to merge it. `.github/workflows/merge.yml` reads THIS file and `scripts/merge/gate.mjs` from the BASE branch — never from the pull request under evaluation — and re-derives the one rule with teeth from evidence: the prohibited-path scan of the real diff. A prohibited path means Brian merges it by hand; anything else gets GitHub's own auto-merge enabled, and GitHub merges it when the required checks are green. There are no lanes, no labels, no eligibility classes and no receipt. Draft state is the readiness gate, and no workflow lifts a draft.
_requiredChecksNote: The job `name:` values in .github/workflows/ci.yml. GitHub's branch protection is what actually holds auto-merge until these are green; this list is a second, independently checked-in copy, used by the Mission Lead before it lifts a draft and by tests, so that renaming a job in ci.yml without updating branch protection fails a test instead of silently emptying the gate.

_prohibitedNote: The only rule with teeth, and it does not expand (LAN-209). Every path here is judged from the real diff — a rename on both its names — and a match means the pull request never gets auto-merge enabled at all. An empty diff is refused: there is nothing to merge, so nothing merges.
_visualSurfacesNote: The coherence tripwire: a receipt claiming nonvisual work is refused when the diff touches any of these, so ADR 0020's live visual review cannot be skipped by mislabelling. Plain .ts files under src/app are included deliberately — presentation shaping and user-visible copy live there too.

reviewContract._purpose: The path classifiers that generate a package review contract in scripts/mission/lib/review-contract.mjs. They decide which capabilities and jobs an invocation must carry; the Mission Lead may add a diagnostic question but may never remove what these produce.
reviewContract._sensitiveSurfacesNote: Auth, authorization, schema, privileged clients, public token issuance, production procedure and workflow surfaces. A non-empty intersection always requires a fresh reviewer.
reviewContract._databaseSurfacesNote: Behaviour whose acceptance depends on rows. A non-empty intersection requires the database and database-reset-seed capabilities and live job evidence; static reasoning cannot clear it.
reviewContract._publicSurfacesNote: Token and answer flows reachable without a session. They require a public browser context and the scanner and reload negative jobs.
reviewContract._transportSurfacesNote: The provider/local transport seam. Changing it requires the seam capability so delivery is exercised against the local transport rather than reasoned about.
reviewContract._evidenceSurfacesNote: Seed and fixture sources. A change here alters what every later proof is measured against, so it is review-affecting even when no component changed; deterministic clearance is refused.
